title: Diffusion Limit and Treatment-Effect Inference for First-Entry Pair-Switching Rerandomization
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is a functional limit, first-entry law, clipped-Gaussian endpoint, and conservative ATE inference theorem for the bounded fixed-dimension, fixed-threshold, equal-allocation subclass, not for the full Zhu--Liu algorithmic domain.

The inference result proves sequencewise asymptotic coverage through a worst-compatible-residual envelope; it neither identifies the residual variance nor establishes efficiency, optimality, or finite-sample validity.

proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived the actual-filtration predictable characteristics, joint stopped diffusion, clipped-Gaussian entrance law, proposal/accepted-clock comparison, heterogeneous-effect ATE limit, stopped-moment consistency, and variance-envelope inference; the Li--Ding balanced-allocation vector CLT citation was independently verified from the authors' arXiv source. D0.5 stopped at triage because the fixed-dimensional, fixed-threshold, equal-allocation regular subclass and worst-compatible-residual envelope cap the package at subfield tier, below the field floor. The listed dependency, scope, clock-horizon, negative-target, and related-work findings were intentionally left unrepaired once the tier was found unsalvageable within scope and must be resolved before reusing these claims.
tldr: Original equal-allocation first-entry PSRR has an outcome-free allocation limit on a regular bounded covariate-design class: the proposal-time chain converges to an exterior radial diffusion, its first-entry time has an explicit Tricomi-\(U\) Laplace transform, and its all-proposal count exceeds its accepted-switch count by only \(O_{\Pr}(\sqrt n)\). The terminal imbalance is a radially clipped Gaussian, independent of a stationary Gaussian outcome-residual coordinate on the smaller outcome-inference subclass. Fixed finite tuning changes the search-time law but not the first-order endpoint law. On the outcome subclass, stopped-arm moments consistently estimate the inputs to a computable variance-envelope interval for the finite-population ATE, with the stated fully interacted corollary.
gap: Zhu and Liu's Algorithm 1 proves equal-allocation unbiasedness and Fisher validity but explicitly leaves common-statistic asymptotics open. Fiksel gives a Fisher-exact covariate-adjusted randomization-inversion interval, while uniform-rerandomization theory conditions a Gaussian inside the balance region and the 2026 follow-up changes the design by running toward stationarity and applying a correction; none gives sequencewise weak-null inference from one original-PSRR first-entry run.
fill: The paper derives eventual nonemptiness of the acceptable set from Gaussian initialization, establishes pre-entry actual-filtration predictable characteristics with a separate terminal-crossing transfer, obtains a stopped diffusion and radial entrance law, proves stopped-arm moment consistency, constructs a worst-compatible-residual critical value, and gives a fully interacted Gaussian corollary without Markovian projected scores or outcome-residual independence.
